newsitem.title: USA: US Southeast power prices remain strong on outages.
newsitem.headline: US Southeast power prices remain strong on outages.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices in the southeastern U.S. remained strong Thursday in sporadic trading, supported by the recent heat in the region and extensive outages, market sources said.
"It's all these outages, and it's been hot the last two days. The effects of the heat always seem to be delayed by about two days," said one power marketer.
Hourly prices for electricity among Florida's utilities were volatile, soaring as high as $38.00 a megawatt hour (MWh), traders said.

At the Georgia/Florida border, firm, peak electricity for Thursday delivery was still strong in the $25.00-26.00 MWh range for 16-hour blocks, with more deals concentrated at the higher end of the range.
Firm, off-peak power for next-day delivery at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally valued at $15.00-$18.00.

Adding support to prices was the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's early Thursday news that Duke Power Co's two McGuire nuclear units in Cornelius, N.C., were shutting down, removing a combined 2,258 megawatts (MW) from the market.

In conjunction with these outages, Duke Power also said earlier its three Oconee nuclear units in Seneca, N.C., with a combined generating capacity of 2,538 MW, would not restart as scheduled in mid-November. A new restart date was not available.

In the northwestern part of Tennessee Valley Authority's (TVA) territory, firm, peak electricity for next-day delivery was assessed steady to higher in the $18.00-21.00 area, but most avoided the market because of the outages.
TVA's 1,065 MW Browns Ferry 2 nuclear power unit in Decatur, Ala., is still not producing power after being shut early Wednesday.
The restart of the unit was not known. TVA's Browns Ferry 3 unit is operating at full power.
The restart of TVA's 1,148 MW Sequoyah nuclear unit 2 in Soddy Daisy, Tenn., was also still unknown.
According to Weather Service Corp, Southeast temperatures are expected to dip to four to 10 degrees below-normal this weekend.
Separately, Entergy's 840 MW Independence 2 coal-fired unit in Newark, Ark., will shut down Sunday for one week to repair a tube leak, the company said earlier Thursday.
